messages:
Maria (PM): FYI — customer AC hit a quality regression after yesterday's model swap. I'm proposing a temporary 'hotpatch rollforward' priority lane in the catalog so we can fast-track a compat adapter + controlled rollout. Need criteria and owners.
Kev (Eng): Can you share the failure surface? latency/regression type? which model variant?
Maria (PM): It's an answer hallucination spike on search results for their vertical. A smaller 8B variant (v2.1) regressed after we swapped pins. Latency fine. Impact = a handful of customers but one enterprise SLA flagged it.
Jia (ML): We should require a focused eval set (50-100 queries from their corpus) + model-quality delta < 2% for key metrics. Also smoke test for tokenization edgecases.
Olivia (CS): Customer expects a timeline and opt-in path. If we expose a 'hotpatch' toggle they can opt into the patched variant while we validate broadly. We'll need comm templates.
Sam (Sales): Does this require reserved capacity? If so we need to surface cost to the AE — customer may accept a surcharge for priority lane.
Kev (Eng): Implementation notes: add a feature-flagged catalog lane (hotpatch-priority) that bypasses normal onboarding queue and pins the variant with TTL and short rollback window. Need to ensure routing layer honors priority policy.
Maria (PM): Proposed rollout: canary 1% (1h) -> 5% (2h) -> 25% (4h) -> 100% (manual). Automated rollback triggers: error-rate > 1.5x baseline OR quality-regression on eval set > 2%.
Kev (Eng): Sounds good. Need a simple rollout policy JSON for ops.
Jia (ML): I'll own the eval harness. I'll run quick quality/latency benches and produce a short report within 3 hours.
Maria (PM): Draft rollout policy (example):
```
{
  "lane": "hotpatch-priority",
  "canary_steps": ["1%:1h","5%:2h","25%:4h"],
  "rollback_triggers": ["error_rate>1.5x","eval_delta>2%"],
  "pin_ttl": "72h",
  "auto_promote": false
}
```
Kev (Eng): We'll need to disable automated pin pruning and any nightly catalog GC for that pin_ttl. Also add an ops flag to force immediate rollback.
Olivia (CS): I'll prepare two short comms: opt-in instructions + post-mortem summary template. If the customer opts in, we must include fallback steps.
Sam (Sales): If reserved capacity is needed, I can push a short addendum to the contract. Let's not block the rollout on it — use burst capacity first and decide after canary.
Kev (Eng): Ops checklist for me: routing rule change, pin API call, disable prune, add metric hooks (latency, 95p, error-rate, custom QA metric). ETA 2h.
Jia (ML): Eval commands I'll run:
```
# run smoke eval
python eval/harness.py --model model:v2.1-hotpatch --dataset corp_ac_samples.json --metrics qa_score,bleu,latency
# quick tokenization edgecases
python eval/token_check.py --model model:v2.1-hotpatch --cases cases.json
```
Maria (PM): Owners: Kev = runtime + rollout, Jia = evals + quality gate, Olivia = comms & customer opt-in flow, Sam = commercial + capacity. I will coordinate with legal if we need an SLA exception.
Olivia (CS): Can we add a standard rollback note to the customer: "If quality doesn't improve within 24h we will revert and schedule deeper investigation"?
Maria (PM): Yes. Keep it short. Also collect user's session IDs for repro.
Kev (Eng): One more ops detail: ensure the hotpatch variant is tagged in the catalog UI and API so support can see it's a priority lane. I'll add a flag field: "priority_reason":"hotpatch-customer-AC".
Jia (ML): I'll run the initial eval now and post results in this thread.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated for model:v2.1-hotpatch at 1859991800 — step 1 at 1%.
Jia (ML): Initial QA delta = -0.3% on the 60-sample set, latency +4ms, tokenization pass. Looks OK for 1% canary.
Kev (Eng): Promoting to 5% now. Hooked the rollback triggers to alerts.
deploy-bot: Canary step advanced to 5% at 1859992400.
Olivia (CS): Customer notified and opted into the hotpatch toggle. They want hourly updates for the first 6 hours.
Sam (Sales): FYI customer agreed to temporary surcharge if we need reserved lanes later.
deploy-bot: Canary reached 25% at 1859993000. Monitoring for rollback triggers.
Jia (ML): 25% checks: qa_delta = -0.1%, error_rate stable, latency within expected. I'm comfortable moving to manual 100% if product approves.
Maria (PM): Approve for manual promotion to 100% at EOD if no regressions. Keep the pin_ttl at 72h and we'll schedule a formal onboarding run to fold this variant into the catalog or revert.
Kev (Eng): Will keep prune-disabled and add a reminder to catalog team to revisit after TTL.
deploy-bot: Manual promotion ready — operator action required.
Maria (PM): Thanks everyone. Post-mortem + final decision due 72h.
